utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then hear from you later. Let's first establish whether the videolink is functioning at this moment. On my screen, I see the representative of the Registry in an environment not being one of our courtrooms.

utterances.text: Mr. Monkhouse, can you hear me and can you see me?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I can hear you and see you loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Monkhouse, please be seated. Could I ask you, in the room where you're in at this moment, are you alone for the time being?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour. He's on stand-by. I'll have him come in the room momentarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon. I was informed, Mr. Monkhouse, that the person sitting next to you is Mr. Theodore Tax. Before I address him, I'd like to turn into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tax, could you please --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Monkhouse.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Excuse me. I'm sorry for the interruption. I need to let you know that we're no longer receiving audio from The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we -- I don't know whether you are able to lip-read, but we'll wait and restore the audio before we continue. THE DIRECTOR: Sean, you're muted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see on our screen that the microphone is crossed out. Do you now hear us?

utterances.text: [Via videolink] No.

utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, unfortunately we're still not receiving any audio from The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we're in the hands of the technicians. THE DIRECTOR: Do you hear us now, Sean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still nothing? I suggest that we wait for another two minutes. If then the videolink has not been restored, that we'll adjourn but remain stand-by until we receive a message that the videolink is functioning again. What we also could do is to address a few other procedural matters while waiting. I suggest to the parties that we continue -- continue with a few procedural matters and that as soon as the videolink has been restored, that the Chamber is informed so that we can directly -- immediately then move to the videolink again. The Chamber would first like to deliver the reasons for the decision on the Prosecution's application for protective measures for Witness 28. These are the reasons for the Chamber's decision granting the protective measures of face and voice distortion and a pseudonym for Witness 28. I am now surprised by someone apparently calling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have to switch our plugs. So therefore I repeat, the Chamber would now like to give reasons for its decision granting the protective measures of face and voice distortion and a pseudonym for Witness 28 on the 1st of November, 2007. On the 1st of November, 2007, the Prosecution applied for the previously mentioned protective measures for Witness 28. To back its application, the Prosecution referred to a former motion of the witness in which she requested to quash a subpoena and, in the alternative, to testify in closed session. The motion provided that the NGO for which the witness works had received threats including - and I quote - "ugly letters" - unquote, and a threatening phone call after the NGO had published an article in February 2007 on certain well-known public figures in Kosovo. In connection with this, an e-mail with photographs of the Kosovo staff of this NGO was also sent in August 2007 to a wide range of persons labeling the staff "traitors" and "spies." While Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Brahimaj remained neutral, Mr. Balaj opposed granting the requested protective measures, as he did not see any basis for protective measures for the witness. The Chamber recognises that this is not a clear-cut situation for granting protective measures; however, it finds that the specific situation of this witness warrants protective measures. The Chamber has set out the standard for granting protective measures in numerous decisions and therefore needs not repeat them again. Because the Kosovo branch of the witness's NGO received threats by e-mail, through regular mail, and by telephone after it had published an article on issues similar to those which the witness testified about, the Chamber considers that the witness's testimony may antagonise persons in Kosovo. The parties have agreed that there is an unstable security situation in Kosovo which is particularly unfavourable to witnesses who appear before the Tribunal. Even though the witness does not own property there, she does work for an NGO which operates an office in Kosovo. This is sufficiently similar to the situation of a witness who owns property in the area to apply the standard test by analogy, because the NGO's property and local staff are made vulnerable through their association with the witness. Moreover, the witness's employment at the NGO might necessitate travels to Kosovo, which is analogous to the witness who returns to visit property or family in Kosovo. Even though neither the witness herself nor her family received threats, the Kosovo branch of the witness's NGO and its local staff received threats as mentioned above. The NGO's small field office in Kosovo and its staff are closely associated with the witness, and through this association the witness is vulnerable to threats made against staff of the field office. Thus, also the first part of the test for protective measures is fulfilled by analogy, because the threats against the branch of the witness's NGO are in this instance interpreted by the Chamber as threats against each member of the NGO as a whole. And this includes Witness 28. In view of the specific circumstances of this case, the Chamber finds that the conditions for protective measures are met. And this concludes the Chamber's reasons. Mr. Registrar, could you inform us whether the videolink is functioning again. If not, we have other matters on our agenda.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It has been restored, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we ... Good afternoon again, Mr. Tax. You have already introduced yourself. May I just verify whether you could hear us when we were in private session when we discussed the details of Witness 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. We did hear that part, and shortly after that discussion was when we lost the connection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my first question would be: Did the Canadian authorities receive a request for Witness 30 to be subpoenaed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, we did. The Canadian authorities received a request to subpoena Witness 30, and that request was dated 29 August 2007, an official request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does Your Honour require a redaction of what you just said a moment ago? Did I misunderstand what was said earlier about the country in question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tax, of course, my next question would be whether the subpoena was issued; and then, as a follow-up, whether the subpoena was served upon Witness 30. And I again ask you to refrain from any details about Witness 30, especially place of residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour. The proceedings that follow after this country receives an official request are that there is an act, the Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters Act, and that's the proceedings under which we followed and proceeded to court. Under that act in Canada, it's required that the Minister of Justice first approve the request of the state or entity that has been received in this country to provide evidence by virtual presence of videolink, so to speak, and under that act it allows for an ex parte application before a Superior Court judge in this country. Before going to the judge -- or on making the application to the judge, that judge must be satisfied of two things: One, that the witness resides in his or her jurisdiction; then two, that they have reasonable grounds to believe that an offence has been committed and that the person's evidence or statement would be relevant to that investigation or, in this case, prosecution of an offence. So with those parameters in mind, on the 30th of October the Minister of Justice approved the request to proceed. And on November the 7th, I made application before a Superior Court judge under the particular sections, at sections 21.1 and 22.2 out of the Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters Act before a Superior Court judge. The application was supported by a very extensive affidavit, and the affidavit set out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- could I ask you to slow down because our interpreters have difficulties in following you on your speed of speech. I'll give you a sign --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- once the French translation is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] I was aware that the matter was being interpreted, and I will try to speak with an appropriate rhythm. As I mentioned momentarily ago, the matter then proceeded before a judge of the Superior Court in the province in which Witness 30 resides. That application was made before the judge on the 7th day of November, 2007. As I mentioned, the Attorney-General of Canada, who was bringing this on behalf of the Office of the Prosecution, pursuant to the official request, filed a very extensive affidavit before the Justice, and the affidavit really was set into four parts. Just to give you the -- the extent to which the efforts were made, the first section of the -- the materials in support of the motion for this application was a general overview to the Justice because this is, of course, a very rare application in Canada. The second area referred to the offences committed and the potential relevant evidence that Witness 30 could provide. The third area then related - just leafing through the affidavit very quickly - to the need for the compelling of the testimony. And the final areas related to the security concerns and the aspect that within Canada we also could have this matter, what is referred to in the Canadian courts as "sealed" so that it would not be part of a public record within the court system or available to the general public of Canada. We made that application. The Justice granted that application. And on November 7th, the order was granted to compel Witness 30 to attend this day and give evidence. In addition, the Justice was satisfied that there were significant issues raised in the affidavit material and that the people that would be -- or who would be present in the room today would be very limited and that appropriate security measures be put in place for this day. And that was the extent of the matters which the Justice ordered here. Of course, there was also a subpoena to attend this day at this place and give evidence at this time. And, of course, as I mentioned, the final matter was the sealing order. The documents - in particular, the order granted by the Justice and the subpoena to the witness - were served the day after the application, on the evening of November 8, Thursday, November 8, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My next question is: Do you -- when you say it was served upon Witness 30, that means that he received it in person?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes. The individual who swore the affidavit in support of the motion by the Attorney-General for these applications and orders was known to Witness 30 or has been known to Witness 30 for some time, and it was that individual who served the documents in person on the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you have any additional information as to how Witness 30 responded when the subpoena was served upon him?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Well, in terms of that, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I ask you that if any of the information you would like to give to this Chamber would be at risk to identify Witness 30 in any way or to reveal any identifying information, then please ask us to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe I can provide this information without the necessity of going to the private session. My understanding is - and I perhaps should digress for one quick moment - that when we prepared the affidavit material and the requirement -- the section that I had mentioned to the Tribunal of the affidavit material, there is a -- a bit of a history with the witness and the individual who assisted me and swore the information contained in the affidavit to be true that they had developed a relationship and had seen each other on several occasions. So in terms of the requirement to compel the witness, there had been statements made throughout the course of the dealings that: "I would not attend"; "I would attend but not say anything"; "I will go with you"; "I will not go with you." The matter had gone through that kind of -- of a back-and-forth throughout, and on the date that the order was obtained, the Justice was told, as it is stated in the affidavit material, that in the days leading up to the application, a day or two before, the witness had indicated that they would attend in this session today and in all likelihood not say a great deal, answer questions, as many as they could. That's what we believed. That's what we told the Justice on November the 7th. Of course, as I mentioned, the Justice granted the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I interrupt you just for one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you -- if you allow me. You said: "Indicated that they would attend," which is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes. I'm -- I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] I'm trying to be -- not necessarily identify the gender of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if you -- then if that was the purpose, then I understand that you were talking about he or she would attend. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes. So the next evening my understanding was and I was informed that the subpoena was served and there was little conversation that day, but I believe very shortly after service a statement was made that, "I will not be coming to the video-conference location." And on two occasions since, both -- I believe Friday, November 9th and again either on Sunday last or yesterday again the individual verified with Witness 30 whether or not they would be attending, and the statement was made, "No."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then finally, of course, that's what we are for here, that you today could establish that Witness 30 did not show up at the place where he was subpoenaed to appear. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] That is indeed the situation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Now, may I ask you the following question: I take it that all the documents relating to this subpoena will be kept in your archives? Or in your files?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes. Yes, indeed. They are kept in our archives. They are, of course, as I mentioned previously, in the court as well, but they have been sealed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not asking you at this moment any further. But so if in future the Tribunal would be in need of receiving certified copies of even the originals, that they are still kept in such a condition that not for -- that they are available if you would decide to grant such a request.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, indeed. I do have an original set of all documents. And I guess what we would have to do is to determine down the road and not speculate today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] -- on what that application might be or what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] -- the response would be, Your Honour, but I can confirm that I do have original documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Most important for me was to establish that all the documentation is -- is kept and therefore is physically present if any application would be made in the future to receive copies or originals of those documents. I'm not speculating on whether ever such a request will be there, but it's at least now established that the file is and will be there. Is there anything else at this moment which you consider to be relevant to bring to our attention?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Well, having heard the oral reasons just a moment ago involving another witness, I should mention that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, that was public. I was not aware that you were listening in to when we dealt with the procedural matter just in order to fill our time. But you're referring to protective measures. Protective measures -- I don't know whether you want to address that issue. We usually wait for applications by the parties, as an application was made for Witness 30 and where protective measures had been granted in respect of him. So if there's anything relevant to add to that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Well, I would just say obviously Witness 30 is not here today, but in the materials there was a request by Witness 30 in terms of a letter that was written that they wanted to ensure that myself on behalf of the Attorney General was aware of the witness's concerns on an early date and the individual who assisted me in the affidavit made sure that I received a copy of that letter and indeed that letter was put in the material that went before the Superior Court justice in this country. In addition, we also informed the Justice of concerns that the witness had in terms of safety and security that had come even as late as a day or two before the application was made. And we did inform the justice of those. It was for those reasons that the justice felt there was a need to compel the witness and, of course, provide the security measures that could be placed on the application in this country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is then now on the record. I'm now looking at the parties in the courtroom here in The Hague, whether there's anything to be raised at this moment. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one matter that I would like to clarify with this witness in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. "With this witness," I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With Mr. Tax.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- correctly -- well, you say "this witness," and then you say "Mr. Tax." Of course, I've considered whether the information Mr. Tax gives us should be given without any solemn declaration. If the parties would -- would want that, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm perfectly content for my part with the form in which the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're perfectly content. That's true for other Defence counsel as well? For you, Mr. Re, as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Since I understand that the information being given by Mr. Tax is informative in nature so that the Tribunal is apprised of the situation, I certainly don't require his sworn testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we return for a while --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before Your Honour does, I saw that Mr. Re was rising to his feet. If he has issues that he wishes to raise with Mr. Tax, then might I ask that he do them first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question I have, if I could put to Mr. Tax through, of course, the Trial Chamber, is in relation to the service of the subpoena. Mr. Tax, you mentioned a few moments ago that it had been served. Is there a -- a document in the nature of an affidavit of service? Could you just describe to us if there is, what the document is, whether it's one which the witness himself has signed or whether it contains the information which the serving officer or the conversation with the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] At the moment, Mr. Re, I can indicate that I have not seen an affidavit of service. The individual who did serve the documents confirmed to me by e-mail on the evening and again the next day of the service. It was my belief at the time that Witness 30 would be present in court today by videolink. So I did not ask the individual to prepare an affidavit of service. Obviously, circumstances have changed over the last few days and we may require that affidavit to be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just a procedural follow-up to that. In -- under Canadian procedural law, is -- is it the situation that the person serving the subpoena does an affidavit when serving it, and/or does the person who receives it have to sign a receipt and maybe write something on it? I mean, are there two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAX
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Well, thank you for the question. It can be either way. Normally with nonlegal service, in the sense of on a -- a service on another lawyer of -- in this country, normally you would not sign an affidavit but the lawyer would signify that the document had been received. When you're dealing with witnesses or other people involved in a court process who may have some testimony to bring or if you're serving a document on an unrepresented litigant, then indeed you would ask the serving officer to prepare an affidavit of service, attach a copy, a true copy, of the documents that were served, and complete that affidavit. In this case, I do not believe that the individual asked for any signature on the documents themselves but, rather, would be prepared to swear an affidavit of service with a true copy attached of what was served.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is another matter I'd like to raise, but I'd like to do that in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we turn into private session. And, Mr. Emmerson, then I take it that we'll allow Mr. Re to continue and then you would raise the matter you would like to raise after that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. And this concludes the videolink. Therefore it can be disconnected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that we have -- before we call the next witness, that we may have an early break and then hear the testimony of the witness after the break, because we'll not -- certainly not finish it before the break, I take it. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have one motion before us which relates to the admission into evidence of the Human Rights Watch report "Humanitarian Law Violations in Kosovo." And I think, first of all, that Judge Hoepfel as a few questions in relation to one of the paragraphs of this motion.

utterances.text: I have it. It's in front of me.

utterances.text: Okay. utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That -- those are the victims listed in counts 7 and 8, the Serb sisters, Vukosava Markovic and Darinka Kovac are in fact --

utterances.text: There's a statement of -- I think of Witness --

utterances.text: There's a 92 bis statement which --

utterances.text: I'll get back to you after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And then as to the last three names being mentioned here as contained -- as being contained in pages 83 and 84. Gurim, which would be a typo -- a typo in there, the report, in the Human Rights Watch report. But let us say -- Gurim, it says, Bejta, Agron Berisa and Ivan Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That should be counts 23 and 24. I'm sorry, that is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. Is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. It's just the wrong counts. It's 23 and 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Footnote --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The counts 11 and 12 as well as the counts -- no, the counts 19 and 20. So easy it is to mix it up. Are they really containing names which would be referred to in the Human Rights Watch report? If you would find --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, they're there. Agron Berisa, Gurim Bejta, and Ivan Zaric, counts 23 and 24. And on the Human Rights Watch report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Oh, yes, this is instead of 19 and 20. I see, the 23 and 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I did -- it's simply -- I've written 19 and 20, but it should be 23 and 24. I correct that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then perhaps in 11 and 12 where you said -- when "Milos" is mentioned, it's always Milos Radunovic, not Radosevic. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think that's right, but I will check it. I just need a moment to check it. I probably have to do it outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yeah, whereas in the Human Rights Watch it's Radosevic. That's maybe something you could clarify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then in relation to this same submission to admit the Human Rights Watch report, the Chamber found that much of the information in the report is unspecific or not easy to test on the basis -- on what the basis of the report. Where, however, the information is specific and if that would also be relevant information, we often have better evidence than this evidence contained in the report. The Chamber further observes that some parts of the report present legal findings which are for the Chamber to be made, and it's not entirely clear how you would consider findings of others when you have to make up your own mind as far as legal issues are concerned. Of course, the Chamber will have to make up it -- its legal findings on the basis of the facts that the Chamber has established. Now, for the Defence, if the Defence responds to it, the Chamber would like to ask the Defence to -- certainly not to forget to address Chapter 3, "Violations in the Drenica Region," pages 18 to 37. Then a few other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Passing on, in relation to the passage that Judge Hoepfel was inquiring about concerning paragraph 20, it -- it is our understanding, based not only on the testimony that's been heard in this court and witness statements but also testimony in other cases, that the source of the material in that report that relates to individuals named on this indictment is the interviews conducted by two witnesses whom the Tribunal has directly heard testimony from, Witness 28 and Marijana Andjelkovic. In other words, what one has in this report is a Human Rights Watch re -- re-circulation of information which has been the subject of direct testimony from those two individuals and that is indeed the direct source for that material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said before that some of this information that the Chamber has received better evidence, that ... Then the Chamber would like to give an oral decision. It is a one-liner. And, of course, the reasons will follow, but already to inform the parties about the decision the Chamber has taken to strike the testimony of Witness 55 from the record. Reasons will follow in writing. Another matter still pending - and I'm addressing you, Mr. Guy-Smith - that is, excerpts, excerpts of human rights reports you asked to be marked for identification and until now we have 195 up to and including 203. You then announced that you had other reports which you'd like to be marked, MFI'd. As you may remember, the Chamber was not giving you great encouragement to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- proceed with this. Therefore the Chamber has asked you to reconsider whether what is in the transcript would not do and whether you would still press D195 to 203 to be admitted into evidence. And, of course, a related question is whether you still seek the other human rights reports to be MFI'd, because then they should be identified clearly and then an MFI number should be given to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe -- I believe - but I may be mistaken - but I believe that they well already have MFI numbers. I am at the present time considering those specific daily reports and whether or not I may come back with a alternative option, because I do appreciate the fact that there's a fair amount of information in them, or whether or not I am going to take the Chamber's suggestion. I'm in the process of doing that, not right now obviously but it's something that I am in the process of doing, and I will get back to you, hopefully, no later than tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is appreciated. So that would then be in relation to both the numbers I already mentioned and the ones where you said --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- they have been MFI'd. So the whole bunch of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The whole bunch, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just -- I just seek a technical clarification, the one-line oral decision. The testimony to be stricken from the record. It's a technical question. By that, does the Trial Chamber mean will not -- although it's been given, will not consider that evidence, as opposed to delete it entirely from the record, because it is in fact part of the trial record. I mean the Prosecution's position, of course, should be that it remains on the record but not be considered, given that it's been given. And the Trial Chamber just says we have heard it but just don't -- don't consider it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll give you a technical answer after the break. Then we'll have a break until ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we hear the testimony of the next witness, Mr. Re, you were invited to -- to be ready to announce in court today whether you would have any objection against the admission of D167 up to and including D178.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: These are the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I haven't -- I haven't brought them with me at the moment. Could I possibly ask for an indulgence until this witness finishes so I can give you the answer then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so. And then also perhaps check whether D174 is uploaded in e-court. We had some difficulties in locating it. So if you would then include that. That's one issue. Then, Mr. Re, I still owe you a technical explanation, that is, about Witness 55. Where I said the testimony will be stricken from the record, what -- that's not what we are physically doing. What we're doing, we are excluding the evidence of Witness 55 under Rule 89(D). That means it's still on the record for many, many reasons. It could be that the Appeals Chamber ever wants to look at it or to decide whether our decision was correct or not in this respect. But that's the technical part of our decision. Then are you ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I call Ahmet Ukaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is it Mr. Kearney who -- or is it you? I see Mr. Kearney since a long time be present in court again, so I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He's been on sick leave. I'm taking the witness. But he's -- he's second chair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then it's good to hear that he has recovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And it's good to see everyone as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ukaj. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Ukaj, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. And I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ukaj. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will first be examined by Mr. Re, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ukaj.

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is your name Ahmet Ukaj, were you born on the 16th of July, 1968?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In Vranoc e Vogel, Decan --

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- Kosovo? Are you a farmer by occupation?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you still live there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to show you a statement which you have --

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to show you a statement which is in front of you, which has the date of the 11th of November, 2007 and is 65 ter document 2166. Can you please just take a look at the document, which is in Albanian. Does it -- have you signed that document?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the statement which you signed on the 11th of November - that was on Sunday - is it a true statement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would you give the evidence contained in that statement if you were asked the same questions in court today?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it be received into evidence. I have not received any objections to any portions of it from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at the Defence, I see that there are no objections. But it first needs a number to be assigned.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1226, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And it is admitted into evidence, because there are no objections. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have a short summary of the statement. I haven't explained it to the witness. If -- if Your Honour wishes to, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's good for the witness that he understands. Mr. Ukaj, for reasons of efficiency, the Chamber receives most of your testimony through a written statement. But since the -- since the outside world would not know what the questions are about, it will be put to you at a later stage. A summary will be read. That summary is not evidence. The evidence is your statement. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This is the summary of the Rule 92 ter statement of Ahmet Ukaj. Ahmet Ukaj was a KLA soldier in 1998, serving first in his home village of Vranoc and then serving in the KLA unit based in Baran. One morning in August of 1998, Mr. Ukaj saw Sanije Balaj entering the Red School Building in Baran near the military headquarters with a group of men. She left about 15 minutes later with the group of men through the main gate of the school in the direction of the main road and out of sight. Later that day Mr. Ukaj returned to his home village of Vranoc and was told that two men had been seen leading a woman into some woods near Lugu i Isufit and that shots had been heard. Mr. Ukaj went with a group of men to the area to investigate. In the woods, Mr. Ukaj heard someone say, "Stop," followed by the cocking of a rifle. A man named Galani, or Galan, was pointing a Kalashnikov and said, "Yes, I have killed her." He ordered Mr. Ukaj and his brother to remain there and ordered the others to leave. Mr. Ukaj then noticed that another person, Avni Krasniqi, was nearby. Mr. Krasniqi said that he was unable to put the body in the grave. Galani waved his weapon and ordered Mr. Ukaj to help Mr. Krasniqi. Mr. Ukaj saw a shallow grave with the body of a young woman nearby - the same woman he had seen that morning in Baran; that was Sanije Balaj - with a gunshot wound to the chest. Mr. Ukaj, who was very frightened, helped Mr. Krasniqi put the body in the grave. Galani then told Mr. Ukaj and his brother to leave the scene, and they returned to Vranoc. That is -- that completes the summary of the Rule 92 statement of Ahmet Ukaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ukaj, I just want to ask you a few clarifying questions to assist the Trial Chamber understand the evidence which is in your statement and show you one map and some -- three photographs. And, first of all, I want to take you to paragraph 9 of your statement, when you say: "At about 9.00 or 9.30 in the morning" - that's that day in August 1998 - "I saw a young woman whom I later found out was Sanije Balaj being brought into the Red School Building."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While the witness is reading that, could Exhibit P326 please be put onto the screen, and specifically the second photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you say: "I was about 20 to 25 metres away from the school building in which the Baran headquarters was located. She was with a group of people whom I did not recognise. Nazif Ramabaja had his office in the other school, about 50 to 100 metres away." There's a photograph about to appear on the screen. Is that a photograph of the school?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: No. Not the Red School.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that a photograph of the other school, where the -- where Nazif Ramabaja had his office?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: The school that is nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Now, I want you to describe to the -- can you see in that photograph where you were standing when Sanije Balaj was brought in that morning?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, I want you to describe to the Trial Chamber what you saw when you said she was being brought in. How was she being brought in?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: I just saw her entering the school just like anyone would have.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were the other men -- where was the group of people you did not recognise in relation to her when she was being brought in? What was that group of people doing?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: They were walking along with her and entered the school together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your next paragraph, paragraph 10, you said: "About 15 minutes later, I saw her leave with four or five men." And then two sentences down: "I learned that her name -- her name was Sanije Balaj only about 10 to 12 days later when Fadil Nimoni called me to Prapaqan to make a statement about what I knew." Can you just tell the Court very briefly what the process was in relation to your making a statement. How did you come to make a statement and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: I found out that it was Sanije when I gave the statement in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the process of giving the statement? What did you do? I mean, was someone asking you questions and recording it, or what process was employed?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: There was the late Fadil Nimoni and someone else whom I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they ask you questions?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: They asked me about what I have put in the statement, and I have explained in it what they asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "a statement," did they take notes when you spoke to them or did you write something out? Did they type? Did -- was it handwritten? Or was it just a spoken statement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: I didn't write down anything. They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you sign anything?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they ask you to read it before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you got a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know what they did with the statement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you tell them had happened? Was it different to what you've told the Court in this statement today?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, did you testify in a trial in Kosovo against Idriz Gashi on the 17th of May this year and give evidence similar to what's in your statement in that trial?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. I was asked to go there, and I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you about -- when you went to the woods and where you went and seeing the body there, and I want to show you two photographs, which are Exhibit P925. And my question is whether you can identify the two locations as where the body was or whether it was that area. So the two photographs will be coming in a moment. The first photograph has ERN U0143926 and it's got a man taking a photograph and a -- next to a muddy watercourse. Was that in the area where Sanije Balaj's body was buried?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: It must be approximately on the left side, a little bit above.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Above it you can see some bushes. Was it in the bushes to the -- on the left side, that is, to the right of the man taking the photograph or holding the camera?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: On my left side, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to clarify that, was the place where the body was in the bushes in the top left-hand side of that photograph?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that sufficient for the Trial Chamber's purpose?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could turn to the second photograph, please, which has ERN U0143933. When it appears on the screen, please tell the Trial Chamber what that is a photograph of.

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: It is before you go to the forest. I don't see anything specific about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Is that the area where you went that afternoon and were shown the body of Sanije Balaj and asked to help put it into a grave? That is, where you encountered Avni Krasniqi and Galani?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, this is the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 15 of your statement, you said that: "Galani said he had killed her because he had found her with a notebook. He showed us a notebook the size of a cigarette packet and read aloud some Serbian names from the notebook. I can remember the names Vule and Vek. I recognise these names as those of Serb police officers who had I heard were working in Decan. He also said that the notebook contained the phone numbers of some Serbs." My question is: Did you know who these police officers were yourself or you had only heard their names? And if so, how did you know they were Serb police officers?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't know them. I knew them only by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know they were Serb police officers?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Everybody knew that. Not only me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the last thing I want to ask you about is in the last paragraph of your statement, it refers to a map on which you marked the villages under -- which you knew or heard to be under KLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown 65 ter 2171, which was annexed to the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And on it you have said this: "Generally mark the KLA territory from -- KLA territorial control from the end of May until the Serb offensive of September 1998. The villages are identified with a black dot." And you've indicated Serb forces with the letter "S." I just want you to confirm that that is the map that you have marked with a black dot and put the "S" on.

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, this was the map, and these were the areas I knew were under KLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that also be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the "S," where do I find the "S"? I see the black dots, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right at the very bottom. Maybe if the witness marked it in red with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, then it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would you like it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Outside -- no, I see it's outside the -- more or less I was looking for it on the map itself, where it is just below. Yes. That's clear to me. Mr. Registrar, would you please assign a number to this map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1227, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Any objection? No objections. Then the map marked by the witness P1227 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Emmerson, you are the first one to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ukaj, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one or two matters, Mr. Ukaj, if I may. First of all, in paragraph 12 and 13 of your witness statement, you refer to information that was provided to you by Dul, D-u-l, the son of Zymer Hasanaj. And I just want to be clear about it. The information that Dul provided to you was that he had seen not one, but two men taking the woman into the forest or the woods; correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: This is what Zymer told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it also what his son, Dul, told you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, this answer could create ... In your statement, it says that you were told that -- that Dul had told that he had seen two men taking a woman into the forest. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think to be -- sorry, just before Your Honour completes the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. I think to be fair, at paragraph 12 the witness says: "Zymer said that his young son, Dul, had told him." So at the end of paragraph 12 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the witness is referring to communication passed to him. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The only issue is whether the one or the two was correctly understood. Now, what you heard, what did Zymer tell you about what Dul, his rather young son, had told him, whether it was one or whether there were two men taking a woman into the woods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said there were two men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we look at the transcript, Mr. Emmerson, there could be ... Let me just check whether ... Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In paragraph 13, in the last sentence you say: "Dul took us to where he had seen the two men and a woman." Can I be clear: Did Dul tell you that the place that he was taking you to was a place where he had seen two men and a woman?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Duli came with us, because Zymer took us along with Dul, because it was Dul who had previously told Zymer the place where he had seen the man and the woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All I want to be clear about is whether you heard Dul himself tell you that there were two men.

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Going back, please, to paragraph 9 of your witness statement, where you describe seeing this woman who you later found out to be Sanije Balaj being brought into the Red School Building, you say that she was with a group of people whom you did not recognise, and you say that you were about 20 to 25 metres away at the time. I want to put to you a passage from a statement that has been (redacted) He says in his statement as follows: "About 50 metres from the school which served as the KLA barracks three or four soldiers came out on the road, which was very narrow as it passed through the village. One of them was Mete Krasniqi and he signaled to us to stop. He spoke to Hamdi, who was in the driver's seat. He asked where we were going. And when we answered, he said that Sanije could go no further with us because she had to be questioned. Hamdi said, 'No, she is with us.' Hamdi and I got out of the car. Avni Krasniqi was standing next to a white Mercedes minivan behind our car and I went to speak to him. He showed me a black -- he showed me a black notebook with names of people whom he said had to be interrogated and said that she could not continue with us." Now, I just want to ask you: The group of men that you weren't able to recognise, did they -- are you able to tell us now whether your inability to recognise them is because of the distance that they were away from you, or could you see their features and are you able to say that they were people you did not know?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: The road where Sanije Balaj was stopped is behind the school. I was in front of the school. So from where I was, I couldn't see the place where she was stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You did, though, see the group of men who were with her - is that correct - as she was walking towards the Red School?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were they men whose features you could clearly make out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: I couldn't make out their features because people were constantly going in and out of the school. She was simply one of the many persons who went in or came out of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mete or Avni Krasniqi were with her as she was walking into the school?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You obviously knew what Mete and Avni looked like at the time.

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And -- and am I right in thinking you have a family relationship with Mete and Avni Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: AHMET UKAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, is there ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ukaj, this concludes your testimony in this court. You might think that only a few questions were put to you, but of course the Chamber has read your statement, and the questions were mainly clarifying your statement and asking for additional information. Mr. Ukaj, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to this court and to answer the questions the parties have put to you, and I hope you have a safe trip home again. Would you please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And through you I want to greet the three accused for whom I cherish great sympathy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's not for a witness to say, but -- well, you have said it now. Would you please follow Madam Usher --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, Mr. Emmerson, Mr. Guy-Smith, Mr. Harvey, do you have any procedural matters to be raised at this moment? Because we have no witnesses at this moment available, do we?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have one slight procedural matter, which is 65 ter document number 680, which was a photograph shown to Professor Dusan Dunjic during the course of his testimony but did not seem to have received a -- an exhibit number. It is at 7 -- page 7201 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. Can I interrupt? And the reason I did is simply a matter of timing. I had confidently used the name of (redacted) in open session in -- in the knowledge that I thought there was no protective measure in respect of him. But I'm receiving an indication that there may be, and so can I simply - and I apologise for interrupting Mr. Re at this stage - but can I simply ask for a redaction of the use of his name in my question within a time frame and then we can consider it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your redaction will be made. And it's a good reason to interrupt because the time limits are rather strict. Mr. Re, you were asking a number for 65 ter document 680. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1228, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that -- it doesn't come to my mind, P1228. Could we just see it so that I know what we are talking about. And is that photo tendered, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I think we dealt with most of the Professor Dunjic exhibits, if not with all. So therefore, if we could ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think it was the last one -- Mr. Dutertre was very anxious that I bring this to the Trial Chamber's attention. I think it was the last one which wasn't in evidence, which was shown to him -- or is attached to his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then may I take it, in view of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I probably have no objection it to, but I would like to have the opportunity just to double-check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then hear from you, and at the same time we'll hear from Mr. Emmerson and Mr. Harvey. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To assist the Trial Chamber and Mr. Guy-Smith, these are the two sisters that Judge Hoepfel asked me about earlier in counts 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the two sisters with the same maiden name. Then we'll hear from the Defence whether any objections. Mr. Re, could you meanwhile inform us about whether there are any objections against D167 through D178.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Looking in e-court, they were marked, as far as I could see, as exhibits, as opposed to MFIs. Could that just be checked? I may have misread it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please check the status of D167 through 178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: According to the registrar, they're all MFI'd but not yet exhibits in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Taking them in order, 1 -- D167, there's no objection to that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No objection to D1 -- oh, sorry, a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No, these are MFI'd, so they have numbers. It's just a matter of --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- objection or not and admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 168, no objection. 169, objection on the basis of relevance. It appears to be a BBC World report of March 2003, of so limited weight to the -- of so limited relevance to be of meaningless weight, in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: D170, it's outside the time frame, and for that reason the Prosecution objects to it. It's a May 1999 document. D171, object to that one on the basis of relevance.
