utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It -- I was informed that it is uploaded in e-court, so there should be no problem in that respect. D174, objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The objection the same. And I anticipate Mr. Emmerson will press for the tender, but it falls within the same category --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Category --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- of documents that the Trial Chamber ruled on earlier. It was up to 17 ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 174. We now come to 175.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Similar. It's also an ICTY statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 176 appears to be a Defence statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dated the 6th of October, 2007, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's -- look, it's in the same category as all of the statements the Prosecution has attempted to tender given to Serbian authorities at the time. In that respect, the Prosecution submission is if the others -- the Prosecution ones go in, this one should go in. If the Prosecution ones don't go in, this one should be treated in the same manner. So we have conditional objections premised upon whether the statements we press for admission are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think on some of them decisions were made already, but there might be others still pending. Now, what if half of them were admitted, others were not admitted, Mr. Re? What -- I mean, conditional objection is -- well, let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't -- I can't take it any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, there -- you object against admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 177 is an ICTY statement. The same objection. And 180 -- sorry, 178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what the relevance of it is. Maybe the Defence could explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It appears to be a media report -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we have -- if I -- 168, no objections, admitted into evidence. Then, Mr. Re, 169, 170, 171, 172, 173, and 178 are objected to due to lack of relevance. Could you respond to that or --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just on 178 I just make the observation that it seems to be something downloaded from the Internet on the 10th of October. It's -- it's completely unsourced as to where the information has come from. It's from American RadioWorks, but it gives no source as to its provenance, whether it's contemporaneous information, whether it was given in 1998 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that it was-- was it tendered through you, Mr. Emmerson, or was it Mr. Guy-Smith, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That was -- that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Munja, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That was -- I was asking a question about Munja and Mr. Salapur. That was the -- and whether or not there was any recognition or identification of Viodimir [phoen] Salapur and Munja. That's where that document was being used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the -- with regard to the specific objection made by Mr. Re, I would at this point agree that there is no specific date with regard to the -- when that document was compiled; however, it deals with information concerning the period within the indictment and specifically with matters about the PJP or paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you giving up any objections on your side about unsourced -- I mean, it's American RadioWorks. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that's the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's source, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Am I giving up my objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, it's the source. And then, of course, where did the source gets its information from, that's -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If the question is am I giving up my objection to unsourced information, the answer is, no. I will not speak out of both sides of my mouth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I don't have the difficulty of taking a position in one case and in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, the issue might be whether you would not consider this a document which, as far as the possibility to test the source might be very similar to many other documents where objections were made. Now, I'm just -- I'm not playing a word game.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I understand exactly. I extend -- I understand exactly what you're thinking. If I could reflect about that for a moment, and I will come back to you on that issue. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As much as I would like this document in and as much as I think the document has relevance and importance to the Chamber, you may well be right with regard to the analysis you've just made. But I would like a moment before I concede it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You get a moment for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I do not remember exactly who tendered what documents. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think I can assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- because I have a schedule of the documents tendered by the Haradinaj Defence through the Haradinaj Defence through the witness Stijovic. And can I take them from 169 onwards --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- dealing with the objections as they've been raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 169 was a printout of a BBC article describing the history of the JSO and its paramilitary connections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Called "Serbia's Elite Enemy Within."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. I put the passages in cross-examination to Mr. Stijovic and obtained his responses. I do not suggest that the document stands free-standing as evidence of the truth of its contents. And so in those circumstances --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so in those circumstances, the -- the news article D169, we do not press for its admission as an exhibit. I am confident that I read onto the transcript the passages that are necessary for understanding the witness's testimony, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the status of D169 should change from MFI in -- no, I think we -- you do not press, so therefore it could be vacated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm entirely in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D169 is vacated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: D170 is a document that was used in cross-examination with more than one witness, and indeed there was some evidence in the testimony of Mr. Branko Gajic as to the circumstances in which this document came to be in VJ intelligence files. It is a letter signed by Colonel General Pavkovic dated the 25th of May, 1999 but referring with -- with unspecified dates to multiple crimes allegedly committed by the MUP and false attribution of those crimes to the VJ. I certainly read passages of it onto the record, but, in our submission, it's not a document the admission of which represents any difficulty from the Prosecution's point of view. There is testimony from Mr. Gajic as to its genuineness. It is put there, as much as anything, for context and background. But we -- we do therefore tender it, but we're in the Trial Chamber's hands as far as the assistance that is necessary to derive from the document itself rather than its contents is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Re doesn't have to add anything to it, it is -- of course, it's a bit of a different document compared to 169. The Chamber will consider admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 171 and 172, in our submission, are properly admissible and are tendered. 171 is the statement taken by Zoran Stijovic from the former head of the RDB, Rade Markovic, outlining his presence at a meeting to plan --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. We have a problem with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I didn't look at the transcript. The more I say, the more will not be on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it working again? Yes, it seems to be working again. Mr. Emmerson, could you please resume where the transcript stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I think, if I -- I had finished my submission at the last full stop, and the Trial Chamber then raised with Mr. Re whether there was anything further to add and, considering that there didn't appear to be, indicated that the Trial Chamber would consider that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Consider the admission of, I think it was, D170, we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So may I move on, then, to D171 and D172.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: D171 is the statement taken by Zoran Stijovic from Rade Markovic concerning a meeting at which the alleged plan to move Albanian bodies from Kosovo to Serbia was discussed and formulated and allocated to, amongst others, General Colonel Vlastimir Djordjevic. And D172 is the MUP information report which set out the context for that interview and, indeed, the working group strategy for investigating the recovery of the refrigerator lorry in the Danube and the subsequent attempts to conceal its contents, which was, as I say, the background for the dispatching of Mr. Stijovic to interview Mr. Markovic. Mr. Re objects on grounds of relevance. The issue of relevance of that line of questioning has already been raised and ruled upon by the Trial Chamber on a number of occasions. Without at this stage making submissions as to weight, up until now the Trial Chamber has accepted that that issue is an issue which crosses the -- the relevance threshold, so we would press for those documents to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, Mr. Emmerson is making reference to earlier decisions of the Chamber. Any need to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The only thing I say is the -- it -- Mr. Emmerson's submission doesn't alter our basic submission that what Mr. Markovic said to Mr. Stijovic in 2001 is of no relevance to the proceedings here, and it refers to something outside of the time frame of the indictment, which may well be under -- in a different case but has nothing to do with this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But isn't it the case that, again, apart from what weight it -- it may have or may not have, that the whole issue of the removal of bodies, to say the transport or removal of bodies from Kosovo to places far away from Kosovo is linked by the Defence to Mr. Djordjevic, who also attended the scene at Lake Radonjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I mean, is that as good as it gets in terms of the admissibility of this evidence? If -- if so, it's of so little weight --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You say -- you say it's outside the time period. I think that there's no major problem about that. It's more -- that's at least how I understand the Defence position, that if someone who was involved in such a matter was present at the Lake Radonjic site, that this is not without relevance. That's one. And the second is that we have dealt earlier with these matters and Mr. Emmerson is referring to what the Chamber at those occasions decided. And although I haven't checked it, it -- at first eye it seems that he is referring correctly to decisions taken by the Chamber about approximately the same matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Look, we -- we maintain our objection and say it's of -- of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- absolutely no relevance to the proceedings before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then on our list of documents to be considered, apart from D170, is now D171, 172, 173. We now move to a different category, Mr. Emmerson. That is the ICTY statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And among them, one statement taken by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if I could just interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we got as far as D172. D173 is in a different category.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right. I made a mistake. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is a contemporary document concerning allegations lodged with the public prosecutor in Peja by a non-governmental organisation concerning allegedly criminal activity of Vukmir Mrksic, whose evidence formed a part of the - I'm sorry, I'll put that again - whose role formed a part of Mr. Zoran Stijovic. In other words, Mr. Stijovic referred to Mr. Mrksic as one of those who was involved in the collection of information and this is a contemporary indictment allegation lodged with the district prosecutor in Peja not for the purposes of any proceedings, making allegations against Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say "contemporary indictment." I think it's 2002, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it relates to events in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just digress for a moment on this. This is part of a body of material which in different ways is put forward to the Trial Chamber in order to make a point which, to some extent, may be a self-evident one; namely, that the statements that the Prosecution have sought to admit of individuals who were detained in Serbian police custody during this period are -- are -- cannot be assumed to be voluntary witness statements, because there was a systematic practice of torturing those who were in custody. Now, to -- to what extent this -- this material is necessary, given some of the indications that the Trial Chamber has thus given in relation to those documents, is a little difficult for us to judge, particularly since at the moment we're -- we're not quite at the point of having final decisions on the admission for that material. But that is the context in which that line of cross-examination was pursued, and it touches upon one or two of the other documents to follow. But can I -- can I indicate that the document is tendered and leave the matter in the Trial Chamber's hands?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, anything to add in relation to D173?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I would certainly dispute Mr. Emmerson's attempt to give evidence from the bar table that there was a systematic practice of torturing those who were in custody. I have no recollection of any admissible evidence being given to this Trial Chamber that there was a systematic --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. It was in the evidence of Witness 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- practice of torturing. What Mr. Emmerson put to Witness 28, who gave evidence to the effect that she had not actually been to any police stations or -- there was no evidence from Witness 28 that she had interviewed lawyers who had spoken to people in custody or she was able to -- she was in a position to give evidence of a practice being systematic, as opposed to allegations being made and sustained at times of mistreatment against some - some - detainees in detention. The Prosecution doesn't dispute that. But we do dispute the bold assertion that there was a systematic practice, which seems to imply that it occurred with each and every detainee in Serb custody, because there's simply no evidence of that. And Witness 28 couldn't have given that evidence. And if that's the highest Mr. Emmerson can put it, he should withdraw the submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider D173.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Emmerson, we now move on to the other category.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is, 174 through is 177, either ICTY OTP --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- statements and one witness statement taken by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Defence, yes. Can I deal with them individually. 174 -- or rather, in groups. 174 and 175 are both OTP witness statements. I should say in parentheses we believe that the e-court system currently marks D174 as an exhibit. But -- but I don't stand on that, if that has been done in error. We -- we recognise the rulings that the Trial Chamber has made in respect of material prepared for the purposes of -- of proceedings before the ICTY, and so without withdrawing the exhibits, I don't anticipate any different ruling in respect of D174 and D175 from the rulings that have thus far been made. So far as D176 is concerned, Your Honour is quite right, that is a Defence witness statement of Muhamet Avdija, again in the category of material going to the use of torture by the Serbian police. But Your Honour is quite right to say that it is a statement prepared in connection with these proceedings, and so, again, without withdrawing it, we anticipate the same ruling will follow us, as followed with other material in that category. But may I say simply this: That that is a Defence witness statement from an individual in respect of whom the Prosecution proposes to rely upon a MUP statement. And one of the difficulties is -- and I -- I appreciate we're dealing with different categories of -- of admissibility rule, but one of the difficulties here is that -- that the net result is what the Prosecution is inviting the Trial Chamber to do, is to admit and rely upon statements taken by the Serbian MUP but -- and indeed to rely on them as evidence of the truth of their contents but to exclude statements taken from the makers of those statements to say that they were obtained under torture. So I -- I don't anticipate any different ruling in respect of that, but -- but I don't formally withdraw it. I do tender it in those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think that concludes the exhibits which were tendered by the Haradinaj Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes may I ask you one question. Yes. I'm looking at the link between 173 and 176. In 176 we find Vule Mircic [phoen]. Is that the same person as we find in D173, Vukmir, also known as Mitar Miricic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The answer to that is to be found in the testimony of Mr. Zoran Stijovic, where he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just don't have it in my --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- distinguished between the two brothers or cousins who had similar first names: One I think Vule, one I think Vukmir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But the names appear on various different documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- as individuals who engaged in a practice of systematic torture in the relevant police stations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't just have it fresh in my mind, so therefore I asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the transcript is 9158, around about line 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That will certainly assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then having dealt with all the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That leaves D177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Falls into the same category with regard to being an OTP statement. This was a statement made by a protected witness in the Milosevic case who was a deputy prosecutor who in fact discusses the very thing that Mr. Re just took objection to, that being a systematic state practice of torture of individuals in police stations, as well as killings in those places. I understand the court's ruling with regard to this issue; however, I also -- I also know we've had some of this discussion before, and I know that I've been urged not to raise the issue with regard to different theoretical practices, depending on what case is being prosecuted. But with regard to the specific issue of statements and specifically with regard to the -- the manner in which MUP statements are being offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, whereas other statements are being wholesale rejected by the Office of the Prosecutor, oftentimes where they have taken them and oftentimes where they have used them in other proceedings or tried to keep them out from other proceedings because of the very same reason, that being their assertion that there was a systematic practice of torture and abuse with regard to statements, I would -- I would tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, could you specifically on -- on the last objection raised by Mr. Guy-Smith, as far as the consistency in the approach of the Office of the Prosecution is concerned, could you respond to that briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm referring to the evidence given in this particular proceeding in relation to that -- the time period within the indictment, which is March to October 1998, and the absence of evidence on the record of systematic torture, which is what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- what Mr. Emmerson said of detainees. As far as I know - I could be corrected - there has been no evidence in this case of systematic torture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think that one of the issues Mr. Guy-Smith raises is that -- but I have to look more precisely on the time frame, which appears to be mainly 1999, Mr. Guy-Smith, or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I believe it's up -- it's up through 1999. That -- that particular individual who was a prosecutor -- was a prosecutor before 1999. But we've also received, with regard to the same issue, evidence both from Witness 28 concerning informative talks, as well as information from those reports that we are presently having a discussion about, the CDHRF reports, in which, once again, informative talks - and I'm using the euphemism there - were addressed as a -- as a practice and pattern of behaviour with the MUP and SUP as regards Albanian civilians and Albanians perceived to be members of or supporters of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for these submissions. We'll -- we'll consider them all and we'll let you know as soon as decisions have been taken. So that means for the time being that it is only 167 and 168 that are admitted into evidence. Decisions to follow for the others. Any other matters at this moment to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was just -- I was just trying to find the Milutinovic indictment. I've only pulled up the pre-trial brief. But paragraph 2 says: "The core allegations concern criminal liability for campaign of ethnic cleansing in Kosovo between mid-March 1999 and the 20th of June 1999." Now, if I can find the -- I just couldn't pull up the indictment, but my memory is it is -- it is within that period. So that's where I confine my submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And just so that there's no question whatsoever, I am referring to the Milosevic case in which the Office of the Prosecutor and specifically Mr. Nice went through a relatively lengthy examination of a number of witnesses, not the least of which a gentleman by the name of Dragan Jasovic, who was a SUP inspector in Ferizaj during our indictment period in which a series of statements that were taken, that were being at that time -- well, offered by Mr. Milosevic were objected to because, as Mr. Nice put it, there was a systemic state practice of torture of individuals at police stations during that time, including all of the kinds of abuses that have been discussed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not the least of which is the list that I at one point discussed with one gentleman in terms of appropriate ways of engaging --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- in interviews.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- the Chamber is sufficiently informed to -- to take a decision on the matter. Then, Mr. Re, your -- my attention was drawn to the fact that there may be quite a lot of mistakes in the meanwhile uploaded 92 ter statement of Witness 69. Would you please in both versions, both the English version and the B/C/S version, would you please check whether there are any mistakes. It's mistakes in the redactions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you -- is Your Honour referring to the redactions ordered in the meeting we had or something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- again, I have not found this myself. Often something that should have been redacted is one of the things my legal officer writes me has not been redacted. Occasionally, something that should not have been redacted has in fact been redacted. That's about the English version. Now, the B/C/S version, he says also contains mistakes that are, as he informs me, are apparent even to him, who does not speak the language, and that the mistakes in the two versions are not always the same. Just to draw your attention to it, that if you at a later stage seek them to be admitted, that we would know that we have a precisely redacted version of the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We will attend to that straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then ... I'm just checking a few matters at this moment. Yes, Mr. -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, among other things, I was reflecting with regard to D178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what's the result of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I will withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I will withdraw -- I will withdraw that because of the concerns indicated by the Chamber. I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not a concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not -- it's an observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand the observation. I accept the observation. And I don't need to -- I'm not asking to -- to muddy up the record that way. And I think it's a legitimate observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then about to adjourn. The videolink testimony has been finished today. Do we have a witness tomorrow, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We -- we're going to make another attempt with that videolink. We're making -- we're in communication with the Canadian authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't tell you what the result of them are at the moment. In terms of witnesses tomorrow, I should be able to shortly advise the Trial Chamber and the Defence whether we have a witness to -- for tomorrow. Mr. Versonnen is available. And whether we have another witness, I should be able to inform the Trial Chamber and the Defence within half an hour to an hour, I expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we have an idea of who that might be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, if -- I don't know whether you would need any protective measures for that witness. If there is a chance you would, we'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I advise -- can I inform the Defence and the Trial Chamber after we finish? Because I have to make inquiries. I'm not in a position to announce whether we have a witness -- a second witness just yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- apparently there's some -- there's someone in mind. I'd appreciate knowing who that is. I don't see the harm in having that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, we invited Mr. Versonnen to come back, I think, tomorrow and then we got a message that he would be available today. Then we -- also in view of the ongoing discussions, we suggested that today might not be a good idea, but then we were informed that tomorrow he might not be available for reasons urgent -- urgent matters he had to attend to. Then I think there has been communication between the Chamber and Mr. Re about the scheduling. We suggested that -- or at least we inquired into whether he would be available later tomorrow afternoon or on Thursday. Now you say Mr. Versonnen is available tomorrow. Would that be the whole of the afternoon or just --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at the end of the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He'll be in The Hague tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if for whatever reason we'd not find time tomorrow to hear his testimony or if you and Mr. Guy-Smith are still communicating about trying to find a solution, would he still be in The Hague on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He would. But I don't think we're going to reach agreement on that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Being asked to make a stipulation I couldn't make.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I've asked him to make an agreement that he's indicated he can't make. And I -- I'm not like the Godfather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then the Chamber understands it as a notification that the attempts to reach an agreement were not successful. Is there any other matter? If not --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I should point out, just so the Chamber is aware for purposes of scheduling, that the questioning will be relatively short and discrete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And "relatively short" means what, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It will certainly be under half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's for Mr. Versonnen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. With regard to the other prospective witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- that's a different matter entirely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a different matter. Then we will adjourn until Wednesday, the 14th of November, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
